We pulled req_jwt_7781, req_jwt_7782, and req_jwt_7783 through our verifier. The tokens are well-formed on our side — signatures, claims, and audience all check out. The one thing that falls outside our contract is the issuing timestamp.

API v2 allows a documented five-minute clock-skew leeway between the issuing host and our verifier. In the requests you sent, the issuing host clock is running roughly 7 minutes and 12 seconds ahead of ours, which is past that window. Drift that large usually means the host lost time sync after the deploy — NTP/chrony not running, a paused/clock-jumped VM, or the clock was set manually. Pointing the host at a reliable time source and confirming sub-second offset (e.g. `chronyc tracking` or `ntpdate -q`) should bring it back inside the five-minute window.

If you keep seeing rejections after the host time is in sync, send us the new request IDs and we'll take another look. The three we checked here don't show anything on our side, but a fresh pair after the fix is the cleanest way to confirm the contract is being met.

Reference: [link to API v2 auth — clock-skew leeway section]

Sarah

Subject: Re: cursor pagination + created_after restart — expected overlap

Hi [Acme contact name],

Thanks for walking us through the steps you took. Leo pulled the same three IDs on our side and confirmed the read on each:

  - req_acme_cur_5521 and req_acme_cur_5522 — both cursor pages returned cleanly before the maintenance pause.
  - req_acme_poll_1189 — the fresh created_after poll after the restart behaved per the v2 contract.

No server error, no missing events, no defect on our end. What you're surfacing is a known interaction between the two patterns, not a v2 bug.

What you're seeing: cursor pagination walks forward from the last event delivered and has a precise resume point. created_after is a wall-clock filter — it returns every event in that timestamp range forward. When you restart a poll after a paused cursor run, the poll's window overlaps with the cursor's earlier coverage, and events in the overlap show up in both passes. That's the handful of duplicates you're comparing against the earlier cursor pages.

The fix sits on your side: make your consumer idempotent on the canonical event ID (the event_id field in v2 payloads). With dedupe by event ID, the overlap becomes harmless regardless of which path delivered the event first.

Two small follow-ups in case they're useful for the next run:

  - Setting created_after to the created_at of the last event you successfully ingested via cursor (rather than restart time) tightens the overlap window and reduces duplicate volume.
  - If you keep both paths available, it's easier to reason about if you stick to one per export, and reserve the other as a recovery tool rather than a parallel feed.

If anything else shows up that doesn't fit the documented cursor + created_after behavior — duplicates where the event IDs don't actually overlap, gaps inside the window you expected to cover, or any 4xx/5xx on those calls — send us the request IDs and we'll dig in. Anything that lands inside the existing v2 semantics stays as-is; we're not changing the contract here.

Subject: Re: webhook delivery — duplicate event after 502

Hi [name],

Thanks for sending this over. To make sure the retry behavior you're seeing matches what we'd expect, Leo on our platform side took a first look at the three request IDs you shared.

What we found: req_wh_9041, req_wh_9042, and req_wh_9043 are all retries of the same logical event. Your endpoint returned a 502 on the first attempt, which is the documented trigger for our retry path, and the subsequent attempts carried the same event ID. So the duplicate delivery you're describing is consistent with our documented retry behavior, not a delivery-side defect on our end.

A bit of context that may help. Scaffold's webhook delivery is at-least-once: when a delivery doesn't receive a 2xx response (or times out), we retry the same event using the same event ID until your endpoint acknowledges it or we hit our retry limit. Receivers can and should expect to see the same event more than once, particularly across transient failures like a 502. We don't offer exactly-once delivery, and we wouldn't want to commit to it as a guarantee — the safe pattern is for your handler to dedupe by the event ID we send in the payload (or by the scaffold-delivery-id header), and to return 2xx only after the event is durably committed on your side. Retry attempts use backoff with jitter, so the spacing between attempts isn't fixed.

If it's useful, I'm happy to point you at our sample handler that does this dedupe — a lot of teams find it easier to start from that than to reason it from scratch.

One thing that would help us dig in if anything else looks off: if you observe the same event ID delivered more than once without a non-2xx on your side, or any delivery that doesn't look like a normal retry, please send us the request IDs (or scaffold-delivery-id values) and the rough timestamp, and our platform team will trace the delivery logs.
